_meta.description: MySQL business definitions used by the English business-data query agent.

ontology_entities.definition: Active user subscription assignment is counted at the users grain. Use users as the base table and require users.plan_id IS NOT NULL and users.status = 1. The deprecated subscriptions table is not a source of truth.
A paid invoice is an invoices row whose status is paid. Join plans only through reviewed_invoices_plan_id.

A user having a subscription plan is identified directly on the users table by users.plan_id IS NOT NULL. When counting active subscribed users, query the users table directly (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE plan_id IS NOT NULL AND status = 1) without joining plans.

Plan assignment is measured at the user grain: use users as the canonical base, require users.plan_id IS NOT NULL and users.status = 1, and join plans only through reviewed_users_plan_id. Treat a plan tier as a name filter only when that exact named tier appears in the grounded value catalog.

City-based active shop lookups use shop_details as the canonical shop grain, filter active status using shop_details.status = 1, and join shop_address through reviewed_shop_address_shop_id for city filters.

synonyms: subscribers based on their start date
oldest subscribers based on their start date
ontology_entities.definition: Oldest active subscribers are user rows ordered by users.subscriber_startDate ascending, with active subscription status and an assigned plan.
Shop-category listings use shop_details as the canonical shop grain, join categories through reviewed_shop_details_category_id, and use shop_details.status = 1 for active shops.

terms.definition: A user having a subscription plan is identified directly on the users table by users.plan_id IS NOT NULL. When counting active subscribed users, query the users table directly (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE plan_id IS NOT NULL AND status = 1) without joining plans.

Plan subscription existence is a relational condition: use users as the canonical grain, require users.plan_id IS NOT NULL and users.status = 1, and join plans through the verified users.plan_id = plans.id relationship when plan attributes are needed. Do NOT filter descriptive string columns such as plans.name unless an explicitly named plan tier is present in the grounded value catalog.

A plan the business currently offers is an active row in the plans catalog. Query plans as the canonical grain and require plans.status = 1. This describes plan-catalog availability, not whether a user account or subscription is active.

synonyms: partners who are on a paid plan but have 0 active shops
partners on a paid plan with zero active shops
paid plan but have no active shops
partners with a paid plan and no active shops
terms.definition: A partner is a users row with user_type = 2. Require users.status = 1 and users.subscriber_status = 1, join plans through the verified users.plan_id relationship, and require plans.status = 1 and plans.price > 0. Return only partners with no shop_details row where shop_details.partner_id = users.id and shop_details.status = 1. This is an anti-join: use NOT EXISTS or a LEFT JOIN with the active-shop predicate and a NULL check; never require a matching shop.

Potential monthly recurring revenue is SUM(plans.price) once per active subscribed user, not the catalog price alone and not a sum of distinct plans. Use users as the grain, join plans through reviewed_users_plan_id, and require users.status = 1, users.subscriber_status = 1, and plans.status = 1. All plans bill monthly.

synonyms: list the names of all the plans we currently have
names of all the plans we currently have
terms.definition: The current plan catalog contains only active plans. List plans using plans as the canonical grain and require plans.status = 1.

synonyms: plans allow for more than 5 products
plans that allow more than five products
plans with a product limit greater than 5
terms.definition: List active plans whose product_limit is strictly greater than the numeric threshold stated in the question. For the threshold 5, use plans.product_limit > 5; do not include inactive plans.

synonyms: active users do not have a plan assigned
terms.definition: Count active users with no assigned plan. Treat both users.plan_id IS NULL and users.plan_id = 0 as unassigned; do not count inactive users.

synonyms: subscribers based on their start date
oldest subscribers based on their start date
terms.definition: Return the five oldest active subscribers with an assigned, nonzero plan and a known subscriber_startDate. Order ascending by that date and exclude NULL dates.

synonyms: how many users are on each active plan
number of users per active plan
user count for each active plan
terms.definition: Count user rows grouped by each active plan. Use plans as the canonical grain, join users through reviewed_users_plan_id, and require plans.status = 1. Do not count users without an assigned plan.
Maps restaurant search terms to the official database subcategory value 'Restaurent'.

A good or highly rated restaurant is an active shop in the database subcategory value 'Restaurent' whose average customer review rating is at least 4.0. Start from reviews, join reviews to shop_details through reviewed_reviews_shop_id, then join subcategories and shop_address through their verified shop_details relationships. Use the default address when filtering by city, group by shop, and apply HAVING AVG(reviews.rating) >= 4.

synonyms: shops in the city have the worst ratings
shops in trivandrum have the worst ratings
shops with the worst ratings in
terms.definition: Rank reviewed active shops in the requested city by average reviews.rating ascending and return at most five shops. Use the default address and verified city aliases. Do not include shops without reviews or invent a rating for them.

synonyms: perfect 5-star rating from more than 10 reviews
perfect 5 star rating from more than 10 reviews
five-star rating from more than 10 reviews
terms.definition: List active shops whose average review rating is at least 5 and whose review count is greater than 10. Aggregate ratings and review IDs per shop; shops without reviews cannot meet the threshold.

For a location-scoped request for a consumable or lifestyle item such as juice, coffee, tea, drinks, snacks, or food, return only matching shop_details.name values for active shops. Use shop_details as the canonical grain and shop_address to filter the requested city with shop_address.is_default = 1. Search shop_details.name only; do not search offer headings or category names. Do not claim these shops sell or stock the item. Treat colloquial intent such as 'I am thirsty' as a request to search shop names when a city is given.

This request is a literal substring search of subcategories.subcategoryname for 'vegan'. It does not verify that shops offer vegan food or have vegan menus. Use shop_details as the base table, return matching shop names, and use the exact search operation below.

synonyms: hotels that aren't listed as restaurants
hotels that are not listed as restaurants
hotel that isn't listed as a restaurant
hotel that is not listed as a restaurant
terms.definition: Find shops whose names contain 'hotel' and whose subcategory is either missing or is not the database value 'Restaurent'. This follows the case definition of hotel as a shop-name search term, not as a separate verified business category. Return matching shop names and do not treat restaurants as hotels.

synonyms: shops haven't put up any offers yet
shops have not put up any offers yet
shops that have not posted offers
terms.definition: List active shops that have no matching offer rows. Start from shop_details, use a verified anti-join to offer on offer.shop_id = shop_details.id, filter shop_details.status = 1 and offer.id IS NULL. Do not use an INNER JOIN or count offers.

Booking amount means bookings.final_amount, the amount actually paid after discounts. Use bookings.final_amount for any average, sum, minimum, maximum or comparison of a booking amount or booking value. Do not use bookings.actual_amount (the price before discount) unless the question explicitly says 'actual amount' or 'original amount'.
A completed booking is a row in bookings with bookings.status = 1. Apply this filter only when the question explicitly asks for completed or successful bookings.

Discount value is the mathematical difference between offer.actual_price and offer.offer_price. Always calculate it as (actual_price - offer_price). Do not look for a 'discount' column in the offer table.

Savings uses the code-owned numeric metric named savings for selection, filtering, ranking, and AVG/SUM when requested. Include valid positive price reductions, including an offer price of 1; exclude zero or negative final prices and non-positive savings. Do not substitute a single price column or ask the model to write an expression.

synonyms: which deal saves me the most money
terms.definition: To find the offer with the maximum monetary savings, calculate savings as (offer.actual_price - offer.offer_price) where status = 1 and actual_price > offer_price. Join offer to shop_details and order by saving DESC, offer.id ASC LIMIT 1.

Offer discount percentage uses the code-owned discount_percent metric. When actual_price and a positive offer_price form a valid reduction, calculate (actual_price - offer_price) * 100 / actual_price. If offer_price is NULL, use offer_price_p only when it is between 1 and 100. If both price and percentage values exist, the derived and stored percentages must agree within one percentage point; otherwise the value is ambiguous and excluded. Zero-price giveaways are not discounts. Use coupon_discount_percent only for coupon-level percentage questions; it reads coupon_price_p and is never combined with the offer-level percentage. Keep percentage thresholds separate from currency metrics.

synonyms: what percent discount do we give per booking
percent discount do we give per booking
terms.definition: Calculate average discount percentage per booking as AVG(bookings.discount / bookings.actual_amount * 100) where actual_amount > 0 and status = 1. Operates strictly on bookings table.
Coupon-level percentage discount is the code-owned coupon_discount_percent metric, sourced from coupon_price_p when it is between 1 and 100. Do not combine it with the offer-level discount_percent.

Exact state-name comparisons ignore letter case, leading/trailing whitespace, and ordinary spaces within a state name. This supports formatting variants such as 'Tamil Nadu' and 'tamilnadu'; it does not correct misspellings or replace canonical state values at data ingestion.

For a percentage, use the code-owned share_of_rows metric with ONE simple numeric comparison describing only what counts in the numerator (for example, rating = 5). Any scope limiting the denominator rows, such as a date range, status, or shop, belongs in where_expression. Example: 'percentage of reviews created in 2025 rated five stars' uses condition reviews.rating = 5 and where_expression created_at >= '2025-01-01' AND created_at < '2026-01-01'. For an unscoped percentage, 'percentage of reviews rated five stars' uses condition reviews.rating = 5 and no where_expression. The denominator is every base-table row after where_expression is applied, including rows with NULL condition values. This metric does not define ratios between two independently counted groups or conditions on text columns.
General wording about posted offers includes every offer status. Filter offer.status = 1 only when the user explicitly asks for active or currently active offers.

An active offer means offer.status = 1; this status definition alone does not imply a date condition or a shop_details.status filter. If the user also asks when an offer ends, apply the requested period to offer.end_date. When counting reviews for shops that have active offers, use verified joins and COUNT(DISTINCT reviews.id) so multiple matching offers do not duplicate reviews. For active-offer questions, use the offer table and join it to shop_details only through the verified offer-to-shop relationship. Do not use editable_offers_view for active-offer questions because it has no verified relationship to the other tables.

synonyms: active offers have a redemption limit set
active offers with a redemption limit
active offers with a limit set
terms.definition: Count active offer rows whose `limit` is set and is not the string '0'. The value '0' means unlimited. Use offer.status = 1, offer.limit IS NOT NULL, and offer.limit <> '0'; do not substitute a similarly named redemptionlimit field.

synonyms: offers with an end date this month
terms.definition: For a request about offers ending in a relative date period, filter the offer.end_date column using the resolved half-open date interval. If the question explicitly asks for active offers, also require offer.status = 1.

The shop_address table contains location details. The exact column name for landmark is 'nearbylandmark' (never 'landmark'). When asked to show a shop's address or landmark details, select shop_address.arearoadname, shop_address.nearbylandmark, shop_address.city, and shop_address.pincode, using shop_address.is_default = 1 as the representative address. For a distinct count or list of shops by city, area, or location, use only the default address and count shop IDs distinctly. Use any matching address only when the user explicitly asks for all addresses, any address, or a delivery address. For other address joins, use is_default = 1 to prevent duplicate shop or offer rows unless the user explicitly asks for an alternate address scope.

A 'products' table exists but must not be used, because some offers reference products that no longer exist. To list what a shop offers, select offer_heading and product_name from offer_items_view for that shop. product_name can be empty. Label offer_heading as 'Offer heading' and product_name as 'Product name'. To find which shops offer a given item, use the pipeline's text search operation.

When a question asks for the volume, number, or traffic of reservations or bookings, it strictly requires a count of distinct records. Always calculate this using COUNT(DISTINCT bookings.id) to prevent multi-table join fan-out. Do NOT use SUM(bookings.final_amount) unless the prompt explicitly asks for revenue, sales, earnings, or monetary value.

The offer table connects to categories through shop_details. To filter, aggregate, or list offers by category, join offer to shop_details via reviewed_offer_shop_id, and then shop_details to categories via reviewed_shop_details_category_id.
